stories.title: Liechtenstein prince’s ‘surreal’ abortion veto dismays campaigners

stories.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 review – a thrilling airport novel of a game
summary: Last year’s Black Ops 7 instalment was a sales disappointment for Activision, and that has no doubt put extra pressure on Infinity Ward, the studio leading Modern Warfare 4 development.

Fortunately, this developer – like series heroes Price, Gaz and Ghost – seems to thrive on pressure.As you may have read, this year’s campaign is based around a fictitious North Korean ruling family that has seized an opportunity to invade its southern neighbour.

Amid the chaos, a small group of Korean and American marines must help lead the fightback, while in the shadows, SAS hard man John Price makes an unlikely new comrade in his own morally ambiguous quest to put the world to rights.

summary: Clifton Neighbourhood Association seeks disclosure of project documents, an independent drainage study and EIA; demands restoration of waterway to its original width At the meeting, the residents again raised their objections and sought answers from the project representatives.

stories.title: Couple handed down life term for killing delivery boy near Lahore
summary: LAHORE: A sessions court on Thursday sentenced a man and his wife to life imprisonment for killing a delivery boy in Manga Mandi in 2023.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Shahzadi Najaf convicted Faran Qaiser and his wife, Amina, under Section 302(b) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) for intentional murder and sentenced them to life imprisonment.

The couple was also convicted under Section 201 of the PPC for causing evidence of the offence to disappear and each received a five-year rigorous imprisonment, along with a fine of Rs50,000, with a further simple imprisonment for a month on default.

stories.title: Welfarism is dead
summary: PARADED as amongst the greatest achievements of ‘advanced’ capitalist countries in the post-World War II period, the welfare state epitomised an era of widespread social prosperity.
Today, as mass protests rock France, the welfare state can officially be pronounced dead.

The welfare state itself was not a gift from above but a compulsion forced upon ruling classes of Western countries petrified of working-class populations at home and colonised people demanding self-rule in Asia and Africa.

stories.title: 40 years later, Chernobyl's nuclear fallout is not what scientists expected
summary: Forty years after the Chornobyl disaster, tiny radioactive particles still linger in the soil, carrying a dangerous legacy.
